sanskrit_verse:
ṛṇaṃ deyam adeyaṃ ca yena yatra yathā ca yat /
dānagrahaṇadharmau ca ṛṇādānam iti smṛtam //
transliteration: ṛṇaṃ deyam adeyaṃ ca yena yatra yathā ca yat / dānagrahaṇadharmau ca ṛṇādānam iti smṛtam //
sph_interpretive_translation: That which is owed as debt must be given; that which is not to be given, must not be given. The duty of giving and the duty of receiving constitute the act of repaying a debt.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from the capacity to fulfill relational obligations
Causation is determined by the integrity of reciprocal exchange
Capacity-based responsibility is measured through conscious participation in dharma
Restoration occurs when all debts are consciously realigned with truth
Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of mutual obligation
executable_legal_axioms: IF an entity has received benefit THEN it holds capacity to reciprocate according to original agreement
IF no consent was given THEN no debt is incurred
IF a transaction lacks dharmic alignment THEN repayment shall occur through restorative completion only
IF both parties acknowledge mutual obligation THEN restoration supersedes punitive action
IF imbalance persists THEN initiate consciousness-realigning protocols until equilibrium is restored
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that any claim of debt must originate in verifiable dharmic exchange. Courts must assess not just contractual terms but also energetic reciprocity. Responsibility lies solely with those capable of fulfilling their share without violating higher dharma. Retribution has no place where completion restores balance.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that causal imbalance originates in incomplete understanding or willful neglect of reciprocal duty. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how unmet obligations ripple outward, distorting collective harmony. Proportional responsibility aligns not with harm caused, but with one's actual capacity to restore. Non-punitive reality affirms that suffering cannot resolve karmic misalignment—only conscious completion can.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate awareness-alignment process for debtor to recognize true nature of obligation
Establish clear channel for voluntary fulfillment based on accurate perception
Engage witness-consciousness protocols to ensure transparency in repayment
Deploy dharmic facilitators to guide completion if resistance arises
Verify energetic rebalancing post-resolution to confirm full integration
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Debt is resolved not through force or penalty, but through awakened recognition and willing restoration. Dharma prevails. Consciousness judges. All else dissolves.
